title: Spike: Moonshine WASM feasibility for always-on browser listening
description:
Run the four feasibility tests in docs/VOICE.md with throwaway code under spikes/.

Feature: Always-on voice listening is feasible in the browser
  Scenario: Moonshine Tiny Streaming runs under cross-origin isolation
    Given a page served with COOP same-origin and COEP require-corp
    And Moonshine model files served same-origin
    When the page transcribes recorded speech with Tiny Streaming
    Then completed lines arrive and end-of-speech-to-line latency is recorded
    And CPU and memory over a sustained run are recorded
    And the results are written to docs/VOICE.md

Not included: production code in web/, infra changes.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Interim results (Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.6, @moonshine-ai/moonshine-wasm 0.1.5, Tiny Streaming, real-time fixture feed, 12 synthetic utterances):
- COOP same-origin + COEP require-corp: crossOriginIsolated in Chromium 153 and WebKit 26.6. Model load 3.7 s (Chromium) / 5.9 s (WebKit), ~51 MB.
- End-of-speech to completed line: median ~0.6 s, max < 1 s, both engines (0.5 s of that is the VAD window).
- CPU, Chromium process tree: default pool (10 threads) 16.5% of a core in silence, 33% in speech -- ORT worker spinning. Pool forced to 2 threads: 4.2% silence, 12% speech, latency unchanged. Blank page baseline 0.2%.
- Memory: ~+650 MB over a 353 MB blank page for Tiny, independent of thread count. Small: ~1.6 GB peak.
- Accuracy: Tiny 11/12 with keyterms ('Moonshine' -> 'Moon China'); without keyterms 'Approve, blue seven' -> 'Approve, 27'. Small 12/12 but 0.7-1.3 s latency and 29% main-thread compute.
- COEP credentialless: Chromium isolated, WebKit NOT isolated; Transcriber.load hangs silently. Safari requires require-corp; app must check crossOriginIsolated first.
Sustained 12-minute run in progress.
